content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional payment infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or [[LINK:https://[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/coremerch-sovereign-stack-deployment-guide-what-nobody-tells-3|The COREMERCH]].github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-what-actually-4|cloudflare]] Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

PayPal, a popular payment processor, operates in over 200 markets but has suspended accounts in several African countries, leaving [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-creator-built-venezuelan-creators-accepting-crypto-payments|COREMERCH guide to creator]]s vulnerable to long periods of frozen funds. In contrast, Stripe, another well-known option, is available in 46 countries but excludes certain nations. While Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy offer alternatives, they may not be suitable for creators in restricted countries. Meanwhile, sovereign commerce infrastructure, like COREMERCH, provides a permanent structural alternative at the base layer, allowing creators to own their infrastructure and operate independently of these platforms.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

PayPal's account suspension policy can hold funds for up to 180 days with no appeal, leaving creators without access to their earnings. Stripe's country restrictions affect creators in certain nations, forcing them to explore alternative solutions. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy, although available in more countries, may still have limitations or fees that could impact creators' revenue. COREMERCH's sovereign commerce infrastructure, however, is designed to operate in regions where these platforms are unavailable or restricted, providing a reliable and independent solution for creators.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

PayPal's payment processing fees range from 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction, while Stripe charges 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction for most card types. Gumroad's fees vary depending on the plan, but Lemon Squeezy charges 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction. COREMERCH's NOWPayments integration offers a flat 0.5% fee, regardless of the cryptocurrency used, providing significant cost savings for creators. Additionally, NOWPayments supports over 300 cryptocurrencies, giving creators flexibility in their payment options.
COREMERCH's sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a permanent structural alternative to platform-based options, allowing creators to own and control their infrastructure.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

When using PayPal, Gumroad, or Lemon Squeezy, creators are subject to the platform's terms and conditions, which may limit their ownership and control over their digital products. COREMERCH's sovereign commerce infrastructure, on the other hand, allows creators to own and control their infrastructure, automating tasks like payment processing, order storage, and file delivery. With Edge Commerce Stack ($197), creators can deploy a secure and scalable infrastructure in just 48 hours, configuring SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for added security.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The storefront in a COREMERCH deployment is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. It costs nothing to host. It scales to any traffic level automatically. It cannot be taken down by a payment platform's compliance decision because the hosting and the payment layer are completely separate infrastructure. Your buyer experience is clean and professional — a product page, a crypto checkout with QR code generation and live price feeds, and an automatic delivery email within 30 seconds of payment. Every component runs under your own accounts. If COREMERCH closed tomorrow, every store deployed would continue running exactly as it does today. That is what infrastructure ownership means.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
NOWPayments' flat 0.5% fee offers significant cost savings for creators, regardless of the cryptocurrency used.
